name: The Quacks of Quedlinburg
edition: Base game, English rules v1 (file path dated 2018)

source.title: The Quacks of Quedlinburg English rules v1, copy

key_numbers.label: Rubies per droplet move or flask refill

setup.text: Shuffle the fortuneteller cards into a face-down pile. Lay out the scoring track with the flame on round 1 and the four seals on 0.
Sort all chips into three groups by value (1, 2 and 4).
Lay out the orange and black ingredient books. Use the black book page for your player count.

by_count.2: Use the 2-player page of the black book.
by_count.3: Use the 3- and 4-player page of the black book.
by_count.4: Use the 3- and 4-player page of the black book.

setup.text: Choose one 5-ingredient set of the other books (green, blue, red, yellow, purple). Lay out only green, blue and red; yellow and purple wait.
Take a pot (plain side up), bag, scoring marker and flask. Put your droplet on 0, the flask full on the large trivet and the rat stone on the small trivet.
Put 4 white 1-chips, 2 white 2-chips, 1 white 3-chip, 1 orange 1-chip and 1 green 1-chip in your bag.
The last person to cook something starts and holds the fortuneteller cards.

turn.summary: Each of the 9 rounds is played by everyone at once: read a card, count rats, draw chips into your pot, then score and buy.
steps: Read the top fortuneteller card aloud and discard it. It applies to everyone.
From round 2: everyone except the leader counts the rat-tails between themselves and the leader on the score track and sets their rat stone that many spaces ahead of the droplet.
Draw chips one at a time, placing each as far along the pot track as its value. After each, choose to draw on or stop.
If your white chips total more than 7, the pot explodes and you must stop; the last chip still stays.
Once per round you may use the flask to put the last chip back, but not if that chip exploded the pot.
Evaluation: roll the bonus die if eligible, resolve chip actions, take rubies, then score points or buy chips. Finally spend rubies and pass the cards on.

round_end: Spend rubies as you wish: 2 rubies move your droplet 1 space, 2 rubies refill your flask.
Take the rat stone out of the pot. Pass the fortuneteller cards clockwise; that player starts next round and the flame moves on.
Before round 2 reveal the yellow book, before round 3 the purple book, and before round 6 everyone adds 1 white 1-chip to their bag.
end: After round 9. In the last round everyone draws together on the command 'Stir!'. After it you may buy 1 victory point for 5 coins or 2 rubies, as often as you like.

scoring.text: Your scoring field is the one just after your last chip, even if the pot exploded.
Bonus die: the non-exploded player with the highest field (ties by furthest chip) rolls it. Tied players all roll.
Then resolve black, green and purple chip actions, starting with the start player.
Get a ruby if your field shows one.
Exploded pots choose either the victory points or the coins of their field. Others take both.
Buy 1 or 2 chips of different colours with your coins. Spare coins are lost.
The player furthest along the scoring track wins.

tiebreak: The player with the fullest pot in the last round; otherwise the tie stands.

missed.text: Only white chips count towards the explosion total; other colours never do.
An exploded pot still gets the field's rubies and can take points or coins, but not both, and cannot roll the bonus die.
Never look into your bag. Players who stop lay their bag on the table.
Chip actions are optional, and blue, red and yellow work immediately; green, purple and black work at round end.
You can buy at most 2 chips per round, and they must be different colours.
The flask can be used once per round and must be refilled with rubies.

not_covered: Detailed effects and costs of every ingredient book (the final pages)
Point, ruby and coin values per pot field (printed on the pot board)
unverified: Publisher is not named in the rulebook text; Schmidt Spiele is the original publisher per search listings
